Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

for the final checklist include the polling interval the separate 250 megabyte batch limit the 18 batch daily planning target the three retries after the initial attempt the 30 second pause the 48 hour cache period and the five batch history limit make clear which numbers describe limits schedules or counts retain the condition about pausing if file status is uncertain and leave the vendor's duplicate file question unanswered after the review staff will note any observed behavior in the pilot log the log should include the time the workstation name and whether the batch was a test batch or an ordinary upload no extra recommendation is needed after those fields are recorded end dictation", "output": "We are setting up the desktop uploader for the West Annex archive, and this is the first week of the pilot, not a production migration. The team has six staff accounts and two shared workstations: one at the intake desk and one in the scanning room. The uploader will send completed batches to the archive team's staging folder on the internal server. The folder is called West Annex Intake, and the server address is already saved in the app. The request is to configure the desktop client, not to change permissions on the server or reorganize the existing folders. The archive coordinator said, “We need the upload screen to be simple enough for a volunteer to use without guessing.”

We will test on a Windows workstation named WA Scan 02 and a Mac workstation named WA Intake 01. Both are connected to the office network, but the Mac sometimes sleeps during lunch. The Windows machine stays logged in at the intake desk until the last shift leaves. We have a 250-megabyte file limit for each scan batch and a daily target of 18 batches. The limit is per batch, not per individual image. A batch usually contains between 12 and 35 images. The scans are mostly PDF files, with a few JPEG receipts, and the current naming pattern starts with the date, then the collection code, then a four-digit sequence. The sample name is 2025-04-16-MAP-0038.pdf. Please keep that sample unchanged in the setup notes because staff use it when checking filenames.

For the upload settings, we want the client to check for new files every 10 minutes and show a visible notification when a batch completes. The notification should include the destination folder and the batch name, but not the full server address. We do not want a sound alert because the scanning room is also used for interviews. The progress display should show transferred size as well as percentage, and it should keep the last five completed batches in the local history. The history is for troubleshooting only and should not become a second copy of the scans. The local cache can retain unfinished transfers for up to 48 hours; then staff will review and clear them on Monday morning. If the network is unavailable, the client should wait rather than repeatedly opening a connection.

There is one setting whose exact key needs to go into the configuration request on its own line:
transfer.allow_resume
Please enable that setting so a transfer interrupted by a short network drop can continue from the point it stopped rather than starting over. The setting applies to uploads only and does not change how files are edited or saved locally. We have not yet tested a complete interruption and recovery, so the setup note should describe the intended behavior without saying that the test has passed. The coordinator asked whether resuming would create duplicate files, and the answer is not known for this client yet. Please leave that question open for the vendor instead of treating it as resolved.

We need a retry policy for ordinary connection failures. The client should make three retries with a pause of 30 seconds between attempts. If all three retries fail, it should leave the batch in the queue and show a warning for the next staff member. The retry count refers to attempts after the first upload attempt, so there can be four attempts in total. Do not delete or rename a queued file after a failure. A staff member may move it manually once the network issue is understood. If a file exceeds the 250-megabyte batch limit, the uploader should display a separate limit warning and leave the batch untouched. This limit warning is not the same as the connection warning and should not trigger retries.

1. Account and access: Use the shared uploader account already created by the archive administrator. Do not save its password in a printed checklist. The two workstations should use the same destination and settings but retain separate local histories.

2. Schedule and status: Keep automatic checks at 10-minute intervals and show a completion notification only after every file in that batch has arrived in staging. If one file is still transferring, the batch is not complete.

3. File handling: Preserve the original filenames and do not compress the scans during upload. The archive staff will perform any renaming or format conversion after the files have been received.

4. Recovery test: Run one normal upload on each workstation, then briefly disconnect the network during a small test batch and observe whether the client resumes. If it does not resume, record what happened and contact the vendor. Do not run this interruption test with a live collection.

Friday afternoon is the first review time with the coordinator, and the vendor representative may join by video if available. The date is Friday, April 18, and the review should take about 25 minutes. Bring the two workstation names, the sample filename, and a screenshot of the settings page. We also need to ask the vendor whether the local history can be exported without copying the underlying scans. That is a question for the meeting, not a requirement for the pilot. The coordinator said, “If the notification names the batch clearly, we can match it against the paper intake log.” Do not promise that export is available before we receive an answer.

If the uploader cannot distinguish a failed file from a completed file, the team should pause the pilot and report the behavior to the coordinator before processing the next collection. This condition matters because the daily target of 18 batches is only a planning number, and it is not a reason to send a batch with uncertain status. The intake log remains the staff's record of what was scanned, and the local history is only a troubleshooting aid. The archive administrator will decide separately whether the pilot can continue after reviewing any issue. No one has approved a production rollout, and the setup request should remain limited to these two workstations and the West Annex staging folder.

For the final checklist, include the polling interval, the separate 250-megabyte batch limit, the 18-batch daily planning target, the three retries after the initial attempt, the 30-second pause, the 48-hour cache period, and the five-batch history limit. Make clear which numbers describe limits, schedules, or counts. Retain the condition about pausing if file status is uncertain, and leave the vendor's duplicate-file question unanswered. After the review, staff will note any observed behavior in the pilot log. The log should include the time, the workstation name, and whether the batch was a test batch or an ordinary upload. No extra recommendation is needed after those fields are recorded."}]
